draft.title: First Nations entrepreneurs
card: First Nations entrepreneurs are Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people who start or grow businesses. Some work alone. Others run businesses through community-run companies.
The Gumatj Aboriginal Corporation is a community-run company in north-east Arnhem Land, in the Northern Territory. It is owned and run by the Gumatj people.
Gumatj runs businesses on its own Country. Country is the land and waters that a First Nations group has a deep, lasting connection to.
Like other entrepreneurs, these business owners spot opportunities, take risks and organise resources. Running a business on Country links the work to the community's land and people.
draft.remember: First Nations entrepreneurs can run businesses as communities, such as Gumatj on its own Country.

a.q: Which description best fits the Gumatj Aboriginal Corporation?
opts: A community-run company in north-east Arnhem Land
A government department that sets business rules
A single trader who runs one shop in a city
A company owned by investors from overseas
a.why: The card says Gumatj is a community-run company owned and run by the Gumatj people. A single trader is wrong because Gumatj is a company run by a community, not one person working alone.
a.clue: Think about who owns and runs it.

b.q: A First Nations community in Queensland starts a tourism business on its own Country. Which statement about this business is correct?
opts: It is an example of a community-run enterprise
It cannot count as entrepreneurship without a sole owner
It must be run by a government department
It can only operate away from the community's land
b.why: Community members can spot an opportunity, take a risk and organise resources together, as Gumatj does on its Country. The idea that entrepreneurs must work alone is wrong, because the card says some run businesses through community-run companies.
b.clue: Remember that Gumatj is run by a community, not one person.

a.best: A community-run company in north-east Arnhem Land

b.best: It is an example of a community-run enterprise

a.q: Who owns and runs the Gumatj Aboriginal Corporation?
opts: The Gumatj people, as a community
A government department in Darwin
One Gumatj business owner working alone
Investors who live outside Arnhem Land
a.why: Gumatj is a community-run company, owned and run by the Gumatj people together. One owner working alone is wrong, because Gumatj is a company run by a whole community, not a single person.
a.clue: Think about who the company belongs to.

b.q: A First Nations community in Far North Queensland sets up a tourism business on its own Country. Members share the work and the risk. Which statement is correct?
opts: The community is acting as an entrepreneur together
It is a government service, not a business
It is not entrepreneurship, as no one person owns it
It is not a business, as it is run on shared land
b.why: The community members spot an opportunity, take a risk and organise resources together, just as Gumatj does on its Country. The idea that it is not entrepreneurship without one owner is wrong, because some First Nations entrepreneurs run businesses through community-run companies.
b.clue: Think about what every entrepreneur does.
